scope: Pinned installed filesystem MCP invocation and explicit runtime/script catalog setup; no whole-milestone or plan completion claim.
problem: The catalog suggested the npm executable with /usr/bin/env node, but MCP deliberately uses the minimal system PATH. Actual discovery failed with env: node: No such file or directory on a Homebrew Node installation.
implemented: Optional absolute server_script makes the existing command select an installed runtime, with [script, workspace_root] arguments. Absent/empty scripts preserve existing standalone executable behavior. No shell, installation or inherited account environment is added.
Catalog form and passive metadata explain explicit Node/script selection and Node 24 minimum. Connections stay disabled, discovery-only and without selected tools until separately reviewed.

Actual filesystem MCP 2.0.0 discovers named tools, reads allowed text, enforces selected-tool grants and review, denies model self-approval, writes a reviewed file and denies sibling/traversal/symlink escapes. Both per-call and persistent sessions recover for another read after rejected operations.

Authenticated local HTTP creation preserves owner-only access and returns 201 using the existing serialized MCP fields. Invalid script paths leave no connection; disabled creation resolves no account credentials.
Optional npm acceptance lockfile pins the real server and dependency tree. Installation and tests are explicit; missing prerequisites fail rather than skip or download software.

browser.setup_save_reopen: passed; command, script/root arguments and empty environment retained; connector not enabled

validation.static: Affected Python lint/format, frontend JavaScript syntax and diff whitespace passed.
validation.counting_note: The locked-server two-case run repeats invocation cases from the 87-test affected backend group. Do not add it as unique coverage. The 165 frontend fixtures are not physical-device evidence.

migration.forward: Additive configure input only. Persisted command/args/env use the existing MCP schema; no record/secret rewrite.
migration.rollback: Existing MCP readers can execute saved runtime/script arguments. Older setup forms can create standalone executable connections. No new persisted format is required.

limits: The real third-party server enforces one explicitly authorized Studio workspace root. Selected read/write tools may access that entire root; this does not isolate individual files within it.
Symlink check is mandatory in this explicit suite. Windows may require Developer Mode or appropriate symlink privileges.
Linux/Windows real processes, personal VM, other Node/server versions and independent frozen-entry semantic reconciliation remain separate checks.
Nuclia bounded-profile/source review and remaining catalog evidence reconciliation stay open; standalone desktop remains incomplete and last.
